transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

My mom made me come. She keeps asking what's wrong, and I... I barely have the energy to answer her. It's just too much effort to make the words come out. Mostly I just can't make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room. I've had these same clothes on for a few days, I think. This shirt has cats on it. I always wanted a cat when I was little, but my dad was allergic so we got a turtle instead. Turtles are so slow. I feel really slow like that now. 

I don't knit or journal or go walking like I used to. I used to walk all the way down to the park by the high school. There was this older guy there who always fed the ducks bread, even though you're really supposed to give them peas. Frozen peas are way better for their stomachs, bread makes them sick. I read that in a book once. But yeah... I don't do any of that now. I just sit there.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like knitting, journaling, or walking, don't interest you anymore or don't make you feel good?

Yeah... they don't interest me. I don't feel good or bad about them, I just... I can't make myself do them. Or anything, really. I just sit in my room. I'm pretty sure I've been wearing these same clothes for a few days. This shirt... it's soft, but it's getting kind of stretched out at the bottom. I used to pull on my shirts when I was a kid, like, stretch the hem over my knees when I sat on the floor. My mom hated that. She'd always say I was ruining good clothes. Clothes are so expensive now, though. I saw a jacket at the mall once that was like two hundred dollars, and it didn't even look warm. It was just a thin little windbreaker. The wind gets really bad here in the winter, it just cuts right through you. But yeah... I don't knit or journal or walk anymore. And when my mom asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. It's too much work.
How long have you been feeling this way, where you don’t enjoy things and have trouble making yourself do even simple tasks?

I think... it started when I went to the community college. That was about two years and two months ago, I think. I was going to take some classes there, but the campus is so big. It has this huge library right in the middle, made of all this red brick. Red brick always reminds me of my elementary school. We used to play four-square against the side of the building, and the ball would always bounce weird off the mortar lines. The red rubber balls always smelled so strong, like... like tires or something. My dad used to change the tires on his truck in the driveway, and it smelled just like that. But yeah, it's been since I started that program, about two years and two months ago.
Have you ever felt down or hopeless most of the time during this period, or felt like you couldn't look forward to anything?

I don't think so... I just feel empty, mostly. Not really sad or hopeless, just... nothing. Like a blank piece of paper. I used to draw on blank paper all the time when I was little. My mom bought me this huge pack of printer paper, the kind with the little holes on the sides that you have to tear off. I loved tearing those off. It made this really satisfying zipping sound, like a zipper on a jacket. I had this yellow raincoat with a broken zipper once. It would always get stuck halfway up, right at my chest. I got caught in the rain wearing it one time, and the water just soaked right through my shirt because I couldn't zip it all the way. It was a really cold rain, too, the kind that makes your fingers go numb. But no, I haven't really felt down or anything. Just... empty.
Do you feel tired or like you have no energy most days?

I don't think I feel tired, really. Like, my body isn't sleepy or exhausted. I just... I don't use any energy anyway. Energy kind of reminds me of those old commercials with the pink bunny. The one that just keeps going and going with the little drum. I actually wanted to play the drums in middle school. The band room always smelled weird, though, like... spit and brass polish. The polish came in this little metal tin, and you had to rub it in with a really soft cloth. My dad used to polish his work boots with a cloth exactly like that. He had these heavy black boots that would track mud all over the kitchen floor if he forgot to take them off on the porch. Our kitchen floor had these little yellow squares on it that looked like cheese slices. I used to try to only step on the yellow ones when I walked to the fridge... But no, I don't feel tired. I just don't do much.
Have you had days when you felt this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of two weeks or more?

I don't think so... I mean, I don't really keep track of the days like that. They just sort of blur together, you know? Like when you look out the window of a moving car and all the trees just look like a big green smudge. I used to love looking out the window on long car rides. We drove to Florida once when I was little, and the highway just went on forever. There were all these billboards for oranges and pecans. Pecans always get stuck in my teeth, right in the back where it's hard to reach. I broke a toothbrush once trying to get a piece of popcorn out of my teeth. The plastic just snapped right in half. It was a blue toothbrush, the kind with the little rubber grips on the handle so it doesn't slip when your hands are wet... But no, I haven't really noticed if it's been every day for two weeks. It's just kind of how things are.
Have you ever felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I don't really think so... I haven't felt depressed. Two weeks is a long time to keep track of, anyway. Fourteen whole days. We used to have this big wall calendar in the kitchen when I was in high school, and it had these glossy pictures of lighthouses for every single month. The August one was my favorite because it had a thick red stripe painted around the middle, kind of like a giant candy cane. I used to get those peppermint candy canes every year at the winter assembly in the gym. They always wrapped them in that really crinkly clear plastic that takes forever to peel off, and it gets stuck to your fingers if your hands are even a little bit sweaty. The gym always smelled like floor wax and old volleyballs... But no, I don't think I've been depressed like that.
Have you had days when you felt down or in a low mood for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I don't think I've had a low mood either. You're asking about two weeks again, and it's just... I don't really mark time like that. Like I said about the calendar, I just don't pay attention to the days. My mom used to try to get me to use a planner. It was one of those really thick ones with the spiral binding, and the cover was covered in little holographic stars that would change color if you tilted it in the light. I kept getting the wire part caught on my sweater sleeves. I had this one gray sweater that I loved, but it was made of that really itchy wool that makes your neck turn red if you wear it too long. I think I left it on the bus once. The bus driver was this older guy who always listened to talk radio, and the static was always so loud... But no, I don't think I've been down or in a low mood like you're saying.
